text.en: Meena saw the ruins of Athens in a book. "Democracy began there," said her teacher.

The classical world refers mainly to ancient Greece and Rome. Greece was made of city-states such as Athens and Sparta. Athens developed an early form of democracy in which citizens took part in the assembly.
Greek thinkers like Socrates, Plato and Aristotle founded philosophy, and Hippocrates is called the father of medicine. Alexander the Great of Macedon built a vast empire that spread Greek culture.
Rome began as a republic and became an empire under Augustus. The Romans built roads, aqueducts and the Colosseum and gave us Roman law and Latin. The empire later weakened and fell in the 5th century CE.

problem.en: Why is Athens called the home of democracy?

text.en: This was an early form of rule by the people.

prompt.en: A friend says The Roman Empire never fell. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It fell in the 5th century CE.
